name: bounded-loop
what_it_does: Sets up an automatic check that runs after every turn, blocks a turn whose check failed with the check's real output, and gives up after a set number of attempts with a written report.
what_you_say: keep fixing this until the tests pass, but stop after three tries
what_you_get: Either "target met at attempt N" with the check's own output, or a report saying why it stopped trying.
on_your_computer: Adds an entry to your project's `.claude/settings.json` so your check command runs by itself at the end of every turn. Reads every file in the project each time, and writes a state file and a failure report into a `.bounded-loop` folder there.

name: eval-harness
what_it_does: Writes tests for a skill, prompt, hook or agent workflow before it is changed, runs each case several times, and reports how often it passed rather than whether it passed once.
what_you_say: write evals for this skill and tell me how reliable it is
what_you_get: An eval file, a log of every trial, and a table of pass rates per case with what no eval covers.
on_your_computer: Writes an eval file and a trial log in an `evals` folder beside the thing being tested, and runs that thing several times over, which costs tokens and time.

name: evidence-report
what_it_does: Formats verification results so a reader can tell checked from assumed: one block per claim with the command, its real output and a verdict, closing with a list of what was not checked.
what_you_say: write this up as an evidence report
what_you_get: A report in a fixed four-field format, and the result of a script that says whether the report has all its parts.
on_your_computer: Runs a small Python program over the one report file you name and prints what is missing. It reads that file only, and writes, moves and deletes nothing.

name: full-output-enforcement
what_it_does: Stops Claude Code cutting its output short: no placeholder comments, no "the rest follows the same pattern", and a clean resumable stopping point when a reply gets too long.
what_you_say: write the whole file, no placeholders
what_you_get: Complete files and complete lists, with a marked pause point if the reply has to be split across two messages.

name: goal-spec
what_it_does: Turns a vague ask such as "clean this up" into a written target: a check command that can actually be run, a starting measurement taken before work begins, and a limit on attempts.
what_you_say: turn this into a proper goal before you start
what_you_get: A short goal file naming the check, the starting measurement, the attempt limit, and who decides it is finished.
on_your_computer: Writes a goal file where you agree, runs a one-line validator over it, and runs your own check command once to record where things stand before work starts.

name: proof-of-work
what_it_does: Requires executed evidence before work is called done: run the thing against real input and show what came back, and confirm any tool that reports its own success by inspecting what it produced.
what_you_say: prove this actually works before you tell me it's done
what_you_get: Each claim with the command that tested it, that command's real output, and a list of anything that could not be checked.
on_your_computer: Runs your project's own build, type check, lint, test and secret-scan commands plus `git diff --stat`, reads the whole project tree during the secret scan, and saves each command's full output into a log folder you name.
